messages:
Lina (CS): Heads up — OrchidPay reporting p99 tail latency spikes on dedicated pool `dp-orchid-3` since ~03:40 UTC. 5xxs ~2.3%. Customer flagged potential SLA breach. Can eng-platform own triage? cc @Ajay @Maya (oncall)

Ajay: On it. Assigning to pool owners — @Lee (infra) and @Diego (runtime). Need logs + any trace ids from the customer to correlate.

Lina (CS): Sending the minimal logs they attached and one trace id: `trace/0a1b2c3d`. Snippet from customer (redacted):
```
[03:40:12] 5xx: upstream_error pool=dp-orchid-3 node=gpui-07 msg="connection refused"
[03:40:15] p99_lat_ms: 1890
```

Lee: I'm looking at autoscaler events now. I see a failed node attach at 03:39 (AWS ENI timeout) and a retry loop. Autoscaler didn't bring capacity back in time. I'll check recent infra changes and account quotas.

Diego: I'll pull KV cache traces and kernel schedules for the affected model variant. Quick mitigation idea: route OrchidPay to a compatible fallback model variant (`rwd-chat-1-medium-quant`) that has lower memory/latency profile. That should remove the 5xxs until infra recovers. Thoughts?

Maya (oncall): Fallback routing is allowed as emergency mitigation per runbook, but we need a per-customer route so we don't impact others. Runbook excerpt:
```
1) create per-customer route for customer_id -> fallback_model (temp)
2) notify CS + customer and monitor p50/p95/p99 for 30m
3) revert once infra stable, open postmortem
```

Ajay: Who can do the per-customer routing change now? @Sam is that something eng-platform can flip without a deploy? @Olivia do we need a release window?

Sam: I can make the routing change via the routing service API (no infra deploy). ETA ~12m to apply and verify. I'll also create a quick PR to persist the change as a short-lived config flag. Pinging @Olivia for an expedited review after verification.

Olivia: ACK. Review after the change. Also @Diego, please open a small PR with the perf regression findings + tests for the KV cache fallback gating so we can avoid manual routing next time.

Diego: Creating PR now — `github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/842` (draft). It includes a perf test and a toggle to prefer quantized variants when node attach failures occur.

Sam: Routing change applied at 03:58 UTC: created per-customer route for orchidpay -> `rwd-chat-1-medium-quant`. Initial verification: p99 dropped from ~1890ms to ~320ms for the routed requests. Monitoring dashboard link: https://console.redwood/monitoring/dp-orchid-3 (private).

Lina (CS): Customer updated — they confirm fewer 5xxs and improved latency. Holding escalation for now. Please add a postmortem and timeline for the permanent fix.

Ajay: Owners and action items: 1) Lee (infra) — investigate/fix ENI/attach failures and autoscaler robustness. 2) Diego (runtime) — perf regression root cause + PR to gate fallback. 3) Sam (platform) — routing control improvements + persisted config PR. Deliverables due EOD today: mitigation summary, PR links, and a postmortem draft in #postmortems. If any blocker, escalate to execs. :thumbsup:

Lee: I'll check cloud provider quotas, node bootstrap logs, and escalate to infra-sre if I hit rate limits. Updating thread in 30m.

Sam: PR for routing persistence opened: `github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pulls/119` — includes audit log entries. Olivia, tagging you for review.

Diego: PR 842 updated with benchmark artifacts and a short experiment plan to enable automated per-customer fallback when autoscaler recovery latency > 60s.

Olivia: Reviewing both PRs now. If all green, I'll merge and coordinate the config rollout with Sam.

Lina (CS): Thanks everyone. I'll keep customer updated and will post the customer's follow-up here. Please add postmortem link when ready.

Ajay: Timestamps recap: incident start 03:40 UTC, mitigation (routing) 03:58 UTC, customer ack at 04:05 UTC. Last update here will be the postmortem link.

PostmortemBot: Reminder created: `PMT-2026-198-orchidpay-dp-orchid-3` — owners assigned as listed above.
